chapters.title: Introduction + How Make Time Works
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening frames the problem as default capture by Busy Bandwagon and Infinity Pools, then introduces Highlight, Laser, Energize, and Reflect as a practical daily redesign.
chapters.coreMove: Name the default force running the day, then choose which part of the Make Time loop will take command first.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version says modern life is distracting and people should try harder to manage time.

chapters.title: Highlight
chapters.sourcePressure: Highlight asks the reader to choose one priority each day by weighing urgency, satisfaction, and joy, then schedule it as the day's center of gravity.
chapters.coreMove: Select one daily center before urgent, pleasing, or easy tasks crowd out the thing that would make the day matter.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version says write a top priority or make a better to-do list.

chapters.title: Laser
chapters.sourcePressure: Laser focuses on creating a protected focus block by adding friction to devices, apps, and other distraction routes before attention is tested.
chapters.coreMove: Prepare the environment so the next distraction has to cross a barrier before it can break the Highlight.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version says just turn off notifications and use more willpower.

chapters.title: Energize
chapters.sourcePressure: Energize treats the body as the support system for attention, using movement, sleep, food, caffeine, and recharge choices without overstating health claims.
chapters.coreMove: Choose one physical support that makes the next focus block easier to enter and sustain.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version turns the chapter into wellness advice or a body-optimization checklist.

chapters.title: Reflect
chapters.sourcePressure: Reflect closes the loop by treating each day as a small experiment, using simple notes about what worked and failed to refine, add, or drop tactics.
chapters.coreMove: Turn today's evidence into one small adjustment for tomorrow instead of judging the whole system by mood.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version says journal about productivity or track everything carefully.
